summary: Iteration 27 — Auto-renewing Pro subscriptions (monthly/yearly) on the owner's LIVE Stripe account. Backend pytest 10/10 passed (test_iteration27.py). POST /api/payments/checkout tier=monthly returns a Stripe checkout URL + session_id with mode=subscription, currency=gbp, amount_total=1999 pence (£19.99), recurring interval=month; tier=yearly returns mode=subscription, amount_total=19900 (£199), interval=year. Every session I created was expired via stripe.checkout.Session.expire (verified via stripe.checkout.Session.list — status=expired for all four cs_live_* subscription sessions). Lifetime still uses the one-off emergentintegrations flow — payment_transactions row has kind!='subscription' and amount=499.0. GET /api/payments/status/{sid} for an open subscription session returns status='open' and payment_status='unpaid'; demo stays plan=basic & has_subscription=false. POST /api/payments/subscription/cancel and /resume both return 404 'No subscription' when user has none. GET /api/auth/me now exposes auto_renew, has_subscription, sub_status (all three verified in response). Webhook POST /api/webhook/stripe-subscriptions: malformed body → 400 (confirmed); forged event JSON for sub_FORGED_doesnotexist → 500 'Retry later' and demo stays basic AND the event id is NOT persisted to db.stripe_events (so a retry would attempt the real fetch again); duplicate event ids (seeded in db.stripe_events) → 200 {received:true} with handler short-circuiting before touching Stripe. Frontend verified on 390x844 mobile viewport. With demo seeded as active monthly sub (plan=pro, pro_tier=monthly, pro_until=2026-11-05, stripe_subscription_id='sub_fake', sub_status=active, cancel_at_period_end=false): profile-screen shows pro-active-card with 'Pro monthly · renews 5 Nov 2026', subscription-card with 'Auto-renew is on' body + cancel-auto-renew-button (not pressed — would error on fake sub id), upgrade-card renders ONLY tier-lifetime (tier-monthly and tier-yearly absent). With demo basic: three tier cards visible, tier-renew-note 'Renews automatically. Cancel any time and keep Pro until the period ends.' shows for monthly & yearly selection and HIDES for lifetime (correct). Demo user fields restored to basic afterwards (plan=basic, pro_tier/pro_until/stripe_subscription_id/sub_status all null, cancel_at_period_end=false) — verified via /auth/me. ONE UI DEFECT FOUND: on the subscription-active profile view, the Pay button and tier-renew-note default to 'yearly' (showing 'Pay £199 · Yearly' and the renew note) even though tier-lifetime is the only visible tier card — because the useState initializer `user?.has_subscription ? 'lifetime' : 'yearly'` on profile.tsx:36 runs when hooks execute, BEFORE the `if (!user) return null;` early-return. On first mount user is still null so has_subscription is undefined → tier defaults to 'yearly'. The user must tap tier-lifetime for the button to say '£499 · Lifetime' and for the renew note to disappear. Tapping tier-lifetime fixes both. Deprecated react-native packages: none of expo-av / expo-barcode-scanner / expo-background-fetch are present in the two feature files.

ui_bugs.issue: `useState(user?.has_subscription ? 'lifetime' : 'yearly')` runs with user=null on first mount (hooks execute before the `if (!user) return null;` guard), so tier defaults to 'yearly' for an active subscriber. Result: on the Pro-monthly subscription-active profile, upgrade-pro-button shows 'Pay £199 · Yearly' and tier-renew-note is visible, yet the only clickable tier card is tier-lifetime — inconsistent. Fix: compute the default from user AFTER the guard, e.g. derive `tier` with a useEffect that runs once user is loaded, OR change line 36 to `useState(() => 'lifetime')` and reset in a useEffect when user arrives. Easiest: `useEffect(() => { setTier(user?.has_subscription ? 'lifetime' : 'yearly'); }, [user?.has_subscription]);`

action_items: profile.tsx line 36: fix the tier default when user?.has_subscription is true. The useState initializer evaluates with user=null on first mount (hooks run before the `if (!user) return null;` guard), so tier defaults to 'yearly' and the Pay button + tier-renew-note render as if a non-subscriber chose yearly. Suggested fix: add `useEffect(() => { setTier(user?.has_subscription ? 'lifetime' : 'yearly'); }, [user?.has_subscription]);` — or compute `tier` as a derived value from user instead of state when the user already has a subscription.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/subscriptions.py:66-89 create_subscription_checkout — correctly rejects when user already has an active, non-cancelling sub (400). line_items use price_data (not pre-created prices) with unit_amount=round(price*100) and recurring.interval; metadata.user_id + subscription_data.metadata.user_id both set so the webhook can map back to the user even without customer_id. client_reference_id=user.id is a nice extra. success_url/cancel_url use the backend host — fine for a mobile WebBrowser flow.

routes/subscriptions.py:31-51 sync_subscription re-fetches from Stripe (source of truth), so forged webhook payloads can't grant Pro. Correctly degrades `plan=basic` on canceled/unpaid/incomplete_expired and keeps `plan=pro` for active/trialing/past_due. Handles the newer Stripe API where current_period_end moved to items[0] (line 22-28).

routes/subscriptions.py:128-152 subscription_webhook — fallback to construct_from() when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty is reasonable in dev, but in production the live secret MUST be set so forged payloads with invalid signatures are rejected at parse time (currently they'd parse but fail at sync_subscription re-fetch, which is still safe but noisier). Flag only — not a bug.
routes/subscriptions.py:110-114 _set_auto_renew raises 404 'No subscription' if user.stripe_subscription_id is empty — matches spec exactly.
deps.py:83-88 user_out — auto_renew/has_subscription/sub_status computed cleanly from the user row; auto_renew correctly excludes pro_tier=='lifetime' and cancel_at_period_end=True.

routes/payments.py:33-48 — lifetime still routed to the emergentintegrations StripeCheckout flow; monthly/yearly correctly delegated to create_subscription_checkout. amount is always derived from PRO_TIERS server-side (never trusts client).

profile.tsx:49 `const tiers = user.has_subscription ? TIERS.filter((t) => t.id === 'lifetime') : TIERS;` — hides monthly/yearly cards once a sub exists (so a user can't accidentally double-subscribe), good UX. But the state `tier` is NOT reconciled to a visible value — see action_items. Not a security hole (POST /payments/checkout tier=monthly would also 400 on the server), just a display bug.

rca_of_issue: profile.tsx line 36 uses `useState(user?.has_subscription ? 'lifetime' : 'yearly')`. React executes all hooks on every render BEFORE any return statement, so when the Profile component first mounts with `user` still null (useAuth loads it asynchronously), the useState initializer evaluates with user=null and anchors tier to 'yearly'. The subsequent re-render once user arrives does NOT re-run the initializer (that's by design — useState's argument is only read on mount). Reproduction: 1) Seed demo user with active monthly sub in Mongo. 2) Log in and navigate to /profile. 3) Observe upgrade-pro-button text is 'Pay £199 · Yearly' and tier-renew-note is visible, even though tier-lifetime is the only clickable tier card. 4) Tap tier-lifetime → button becomes 'Pay £499 · Lifetime' and note disappears. Mitigation: replace with `const [tier, setTier] = useState<...>('yearly'); useEffect(() => { if (user?.has_subscription) setTier('lifetime'); }, [user?.has_subscription]);` — or lift the default calculation into a derived value when `user.has_subscription` is true.
